01.r: The whole company of believers, without exception.

02.r: Adds a further description of the community.

03.r: The article turns 'believing' into a name for a group: those who believe.

04.r: Those who had come to faith, described by what marks them.
04.n: Abbott-Smith: 'to have faith (in), to believe'. A present participle, so the group is described by an ongoing trait; the BSB makes it a noun, 'the believers'.

05.r: Describes how they lived over a period.
05.n: An imperfect: a lasting state, not a single moment.

06.r: With 'the same', a fixed phrase: they were together.
06.n: Literally 'upon the same', with 'place' or 'thing' understood. The Geneva's 'in one place' and the YLT's 'at the same place' read it of place; 'together' leaves open whether it means place or fellowship.

07.r: Part of the fixed phrase 'upon the same'.

08.r: Part of the fixed phrase; 'the same' place or company.
08.n: A form of αὐτός, 'self, same'; with the article it means 'the same'.

09.r: Joins their being together to their sharing.

10.r: Their ongoing practice: they held everything as shared.
10.n: An imperfect, which describes a continuing practice rather than a single act.

11.n: Abbott-Smith calls this a strengthened form of πᾶς, 'all', and cites this verse for its neuter use standing alone: all things.

12.r: What belonged to each was treated as belonging to all.
12.n: Abbott-Smith files this verse, with Acts 4:32, under 'common (general; = Lat. communis)'. His second sense, 'common' as ordinary and so unhallowed or unclean, is a different use of the same word and does not apply here.
